subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
Since this is a vehicle rather than a creature, I'm deciding joints aren't necessary—I can keep it as a static model with parts placed directly in model space under the root, which simplifies the rigging while still letting me build a richly detailed structure.

I'm planning out a six-wheeled carrier roughly 10m long and 3m wide, with a forward-facing cab and a rear-mounted railgun whose long barrel extends forward over the cab at a slight elevation. I'm also considering stabilizer outriggers with ground pads while keeping the wheels simple, and sketching out helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and rods to construct the hull, plus a camo paint scheme using mottled olive tones.

I'm settling on using my own paint and texture functions rather than importing from the kits, picking an olive-drab and steel color palette with orange and cyan accents, and planning hazard stripe and emblem textures along with glow effects for the rail coils and lights. Now I'm building out the chassis and hull geometry, including a sloped front glacis plate.

Working out hull extrusion profile...

Still placing windscreen geometry...

Setting wheel positions and dimensions now, with fenders added above each wheel to cover the hull overlap since wheels sit outside the hull's x-span.

Adding differential housings as spheres, then designing outriggers as stabilizer legs positioned between the wheels, with horizontal beams extending from the hull and hydraulic legs dropping down to ground pads.

Adding a hazard-stripe texture to the top of the pad, then moving on to designing the railgun turret assembly—base ring, body, elevated pivot, and parallel rail bars extending forward at an angle.

Checking that the barrel clears the cab roof as it passes over, and adjusting the pivot position so the muzzle sits around z=6.2 without the hull length becoming unbalanced front-to-back.

Now I'm building the gun geometry in its own local coordinate frame using a helper function, orienting each box along the aim direction with the z-axis as the barrel axis and world-up for roll reference. For the rails themselves I'm defining twin steel boxes running most of the barrel's length with thin glowing strips along their inner faces.

Writing rail and bracket geometry...

Adjusting positions so the turret body sits correctly on the deck with the gun pivot above it, then adding elevation cradle sides and a trunnion cylinder for the pivot. Now I'm positioning a hydraulic elevation cylinder running from the turret up to the underside of the breech.

I'm placing three upright capacitor cylinders on the rear deck with glowing cyan caps and orange hazard bands, connected to the turret rear via curved conduit sweeps.

For the hull I'm adding front details: glowing headlight boxes mounted on the sloped glacis face, a dark bumper bar, and tow hooks, positioning everything along the angled front armor plate geometry.

I'm also planning side armor skirts with stowage boxes between the wheel stations, outrigger beam attachment points, and hatch panels with stenciled unit markings and emblem decals on the hull flanks.

Given the conflict with the outrigger position, I'll relocate the emblem to the turret sides instead—placing small outward-facing texture planes sized for the turret's width, oriented so the decal reads correctly from outside. I'm also adding hazard stripes near the outrigger and a bold "06" number stencil on the hull side near the front fender.

I'll put the stencil panel on the cab door instead to avoid clashing with the outrigger beam geometry. For the roof, I'm adding a thin whip antenna rod rising from the cab, a sensor dome sphere, an orange-glowing light bar, and a sensor mast with a radar dish.

For the rear deck I'm adding toolboxes and an exhaust stack cylinder with a cap behind the cab. For the hull paint, I'm layering olive-based camo mottling with darker patches, plus a muddy brown countershade near the bottom to weather the lower hull.

Now I'm adding a hatch circle and ring on the turret top, a comms dome, rear bumper box details with glowing red tail lights, and a license plate texture.

For textures I'm planning hazard stripes, a dark teal visor glass, a lightning-bolt roundel emblem, stenciled door numbers with panel borders, vent grille slats, a glowing radar-style control panel for the turret rear, and a caution/HV warning label.

I'm working out the plane helper for applying decals, figuring out direction and up vectors for flat versus vertical surfaces, and deciding to use circular planes rather than boxes for pads to keep hazard textures looking clean, plus adding glow to the screen decal.

For the hull, I'm shaping an extruded profile where the outline runs along the z and y axes with set thickness and painted hull color, keeping the surface sharp without smoothing. I'm also laying out a turret extrude profile with angular coordinates to give it a sharper, faceted look.

Defining a gun pivot helper function that computes position along the barrel axis with offsets, plus a box-placement helper that orients boxes along the barrel direction with the z-axis for geometry placement.

I'm checking the cylinder and rail geometry against the pivot math -- computing muzzle height and position at the rail's far end to make sure the barrel clears the cab roof, then tweaking the elevation angle down to around 9° to keep clearance comfortable.

The front overhang is fine stylistically, so I'm skipping a travel-lock strut and just adding a pair of counter-recoil buffer cylinders beneath the rails, positioned near the rear of the gun assembly, plus starting to add sight details and a cyan emissive accent along the gun spine.

Checking overall model height is well within tolerance, so I move on to detailing the wheels: adding mottled dark-and-brown paint texture to the tires for a muddy look, then placing lug nuts in a radial pattern on each wheel hub and sizing the hub cylinder itself.

Adding wheel hub details...

Now I'm figuring out the axle placement spanning the hull width, considering a differential sphere near the bottom, and planning olive fender boxes positioned above each wheel to cover their tops.

Checking wheel-fender overlaps at the front, middle, and rear positions confirms clearance against the hull edges, so now I'm sizing outrigger beams extending from the hull sides with mounting legs and piston supports underneath.

I'm verifying the diagonal brace rods and pads don't collide with wheel geometry, then setting up loops to generate the four outrigger assemblies symmetrically on both sides and front/back of the vehicle.

I'm adding hazard striping textures on top of the beam surfaces, then planning rear deck details like stowage boxes and cable reels, being careful to keep them clear of the turret's rotation zone.

Checking spacing between the capacitors and turret rear, then placing ammo crates and exhaust stacks on the forward deck and cab roof, making sure everything fits within the hull width.

I also need a lightbar box on the cab roof with an orange glow, plus a radar mast with a small lathe-generated dish extending up from the cab.

For the dish, I'm defining a concave bowl profile closed with four points, oriented along a forward-tilted axis so the opening faces outward. For the tail, I'm placing a rear bumper box near the hull's back edge and adding small red glowing tail lights on either side.

Skipping the rear ramp and skid plate for now since they won't be visible against the hull geometry. For the front grille, I'm computing the glacis plane's normal direction from its slope to position a vent texture flush against the armor surface.

Positioning headlights as small glow boxes tilted along the glacis normal, placed symmetrically at the corners while making sure they don't overlap the vent plane's width.

Now I'm working out side cab details: a door plane around mid-cab height, a glass window above it, and a door number stencil below, all sized to fit the sloped cab profile. I'm also figuring out the correct local axis orientation so text on the side planes reads correctly when viewed from outside the vehicle.

I'm placing the turret emblem plane on the turret's flat sides, sized to fit within its thickness, and considering adding a control panel screen on the turret's slightly sloped rear face.

Checking placement against the capacitors, which span wide enough to hide a rear-mounted panel, so I'm moving the panels to the turret's front face instead, positioning them to clear the gun breech and barrel while keeping them at a readable height, with a screen on one side.

I'm adding conduit tubes sweeping from the capacitor tops back to the turret rear using a curved path, plus a recoil-lock cradle for the gun, and defining a steel paint material for the rails using a mixed countershade.

Now I'm defining the dark accent color and thinking through whether I need randomness for things like rivets or mud splatter decals -- deciding rivets can just be placed in rows via loops without rng, and planning how many parts the wheels and hull rivet rows will add.

Tallying up part counts across wheels, pads, gun, and hull to keep the model around 250 parts, then sketching a hazard-stripe SVG pattern using diagonal lines spaced for a repeating warning texture.

Now I'm designing the remaining decals and surface details: a roundel emblem with lightning-bolt rail graphics, a door number panel reading "RG-06" in bold monospace, a tinted visor gradient with highlight streaks, slatted vent texture, and a cockpit screen showing a cyan grid with waveform and crosshair overlays on a dark green background.

Writing helper functions...

Still writing bracket geometry...

Still laying out gun geometry...

Adding the trunnion cylinder and cradle support boxes, then placing hydraulic sleeve and piston cylinders near the breech base inside the turret cavity.

Attaching the hydraulic to the breech sides still puts it inside the turret body, so I decide to raise the gun pivot to y=3.3 with a mounting pedestal instead, recomputing muzzle height and checking cab clearance to confirm it stays clear at around y=4.0.

Now I'm trying to place the elevation ram geometry, testing various breech and roof anchor points to find positions where the base and rod form a proper short diagonal rather than lying nearly horizontal, since the first attempts put the hydraulic link almost flat and unrealistic.

I'm abandoning the hydraulic ram idea entirely in favor of a simpler elevation arc design and instead working out the pedestal cradle boxes that support the gun on the turret roof, checking that the breech housing bottom and pivot height sit correctly relative to the roof surface at y≈2.8–3.6.

Now I'm checking overall gun height clearances and breech rear position, then plotting the curved conduit path that routes from the capacitor tops into the breech rear using a catmull-rom sweep with small radius tubing, followed by defining the capacitor glow caps, orange accent bands, and cylindrical cap bodies.

Spacing the capacitors at ±0.85 to avoid overlap while staying within hull bounds, then skipping cab detail elements like lights and wipers to focus on writing the hull geometry -- adding side trim panels, rivet rows along the hull edges, and letting mud texturing handle the wheel splash effects rather than modeling it explicitly.

Writing the hull paint shader now...

Still writing extrusion and pad geometry...

Adding more components...
